arxiv-2202-00811.title: Kinetic modeling of neutral transport for a continuum gyrokinetic code
arxiv-2202-00811.creator: T. N. Bernard, F. D. Halpern, M. Francisquez, N. R. Mandell, J. Juno, G. W. Hammett, A. Hakim, G. Wilkie, J. Guterl
arxiv-2202-00811.description: Abstract We present the first-of-its-kind coupling of a continuum full- f f gyrokinetic turbulence model with a 6D continuum model for kinetic neutrals, carried out using the Gkeyll code. Our objective is to improve the first-principles understanding of the role of neutrals in plasma fueling, detachment, and their interaction with edge plasma profiles and turbulence statistics.

arxiv-2202-09218.title: Archetypal Factorization and Gluon Poles in semi-exclusive reactions
arxiv-2202-09218.creator: I. V. Anikin, L. Szymanowski
arxiv-2202-09218.description: Abstract Within the archetypal factorization procedure, we study the gluon pole contributions manifesting in the nucleon-lepton hard processes of hadron production. We prove the dominant role of gluon pole contributions in the processes of such kind. We analyse the different sources of complexity associated with the gluon pole functions.

arxiv-2206-01139.title: Self-sustained oscillations of active viscoelastic matter
arxiv-2206-01139.creator: Emmanuel L. C. VI M. Plan, Huong Le Thi, Julia M. Yeomans, Amin Doostmohammadi
arxiv-2206-01139.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Emmanuel L. C. VI M. Plan, Huong Le Thi, Julia M. Yeomans, Amin Doostmohammadi. Models of active nematics in biological systems normally require complexity arising from the hydrodynamics involved at the microscopic level as well as the viscoelastic nature of the system. Here we show that a minimal, space-independent, model based on the temporal alignment of active and polymeric particles provides an avenue to predict and study their coupled dynamics within the framework of dynamical systems.

arxiv-2302-13667.title: Determining the b b -chromatic number of subdivision-vertex neighbourhood coronas
arxiv-2302-13667.creator: Raúl M. Falcón 1,∗ , M. Venkatachalam 2 and S. Julie Margaret 2
arxiv-2302-13667.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Raúl M. Falcón 1,∗ , M. Venkatachalam 2 and S. Julie Margaret 2. Let G G and H H be two graphs, each one of them being a path, a cycle or a star. In this paper, we determine the b b -chromatic number of every subdivision-vertex neighbourhood corona G ⊡ H G\boxdot H or G ⊡ K n G\boxdot K_{n} , where K n K_{n} is the complete graph of order n n .

arxiv-2307-09849.title: New additive results on *-DMP elements in Banach algebras Thanks: Corresponding author: Marjan Sheibani
arxiv-2307-09849.creator: Fatemeh Zamiri, Ali Ghaffari, Marjan Sheibani ∗
arxiv-2307-09849.description: Abstract . We present new additive results for the *-DMP elements in a Banach algebra with involution. The necessary and sufficient conditions under which the sum of two perturbed *-DMP elements in a Banach *-algebra is a *-DMP element are obtained. As an application, the *-DMP block complex matrices are investigated.

arxiv-2401-05512.title: rational and lacunary algebraic curves
arxiv-2401-05512.creator: Georges Comte, Sébastien Tavenas
arxiv-2401-05512.description: Abstract . We give a bound on the number 𝒵 \mathcal{Z} of intersection points in a ball of the complex plane, between a rational curve and a lacunary algebraic curve Q = 0 Q=0 . This bound depends only on the lacunarity diagram of Q Q , and in particular is uniform in the coefficients of Q Q .

arxiv-2405-00300.title: On a new class of BDF and IMEX schemes for parabolic type equations Thanks: † Department of Mathematics, National University of Singapore, Singapore, 119076 (hfkeng@nus.edu.sg). ‡ School of Mathematical Science, Eastern Institute of Technology, Ningbo, 315200, China (jshen@eitech.edu.cn). This work
arxiv-2405-00300.creator: Fukeng Huang † and Jie Shen ‡
arxiv-2405-00300.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Fukeng Huang † and Jie Shen ‡. When applying the classical multistep schemes for solving differential equations , one often faces the dilemma that smaller time steps are needed with higher-order schemes, making it impractical to use high-order schemes for stiff problems. We construct in this paper a new class of BDF and implicit-explicit (IMEX) schemes for parabolic type equations based on the Taylor expansions at time t n + β t^{n+\beta} with β > 1 \beta>1 being a tunable parameter.

pmc-10715030.creator: Fabian G. Martinez, Ryszard A. Zielke, Cyrielle E. Fougeroux, Lixin Li, Adam F. Sander, Aleksandra E. Sikora

Herein, we explored the versatile and effective Tag/Catcher-AP205 capsid VLP (cVLP) vaccine platform to address the urgent need for the development of an effective and safe vaccine against gonorrhea.

pmc-11354524.title: Behavior of Assembled Promyelocytic Leukemia Nuclear Bodies upon Asymmetric Division in Mouse Oocytes
pmc-11354524.creator: Osamu Udagawa, Ayaka Kato-Udagawa, Seishiro Hirano, Dmitry S Bogolyubov
pmc-11354524.description: Promyelocytic leukemia (PML) nuclear bodies (PML-NBs) are core–shell-type membrane-less organelles typically found in the nucleus of mammalian somatic cells but are absent in mouse oocytes. Here, we deliberately induced the assembly of PML-NBs by injecting mRNA encoding human PML protein (hPML VI -sfGFP) into oocytes and investigated their impact on fertilization in which oocyte/embryos undergo multiple types of stresses.

pmc-11366499.title: Anatomical traits explain drought response of seedlings from wet tropical forests
pmc-11366499.creator: Rishiddh Jhaveri, Lakshmipriya Cannanbilla, K S Arpitha Bhat, Mahesh Sankaran, Meghna Krishnadas
pmc-11366499.description: Water availability regulates plant community dynamics but the drought response of seedlings remains poorly known, despite their vulnerability, especially for the Asian tropics. In particular, discerning how functional traits of seedlings mediate drought response can aid generalizable predictions of tree responses to global environmental change. We assessed interspecific variation in drought response explained by above‐ and below‐ground seedling traits.

pmc-11428452.title: Activation of GABABR Attenuates Intestinal Inflammation by Reducing Oxidative Stress through Modulating the TLR4/MyD88/NLRP3 Pathway and Gut Microbiota Abundance
pmc-11428452.creator: Ziteng Deng, Dan Li, Lu Wang, Jing Lan, Jiaqi Wang, Yunfei Ma, José Ángel Rufián-Henares
pmc-11428452.description: Oxidative stress emerges as a prominent factor in the onset and progression of intestinal inflammation, primarily due to its critical role in damaging cells and tissues. GABAergic signaling is important in the occurrence and development of various intestinal disorders, yet its effect on oxidative stress remains unclear.

pmc-12468020.title: Photoinduced Inhibition of Neutrophil Extracellular Traps Formation by Dichromatic Light Irradiation
pmc-12468020.creator: Kahramon Mamatkulov, Yersultan Arynbek, Huy Duc Le, Nina Vorobjeva, Grigory Arzumanyan, Sofía S Jerez
pmc-12468020.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Neutrophils are the first line of defense of the human immune system against pathogens. Photobiomodulation, mediated by mitochondrial photoacceptors such as cytochrome c oxidase, has emerged as a method to modulate neutrophil function through targeted light exposure. Despite the extensive characterization of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) formation (NETosis), the wavelength-specific modulation of neutrophil photoactivation and the involvement of redox pathways remain poorly defined.

pmc-12554055.title: Critical limb ischemia leading to amputation as a presentation of acquired hemophilia A with congenital factor XII deficiency: a case report
pmc-12554055.creator: Lam Van Nut, Duong Dinh Bao, Bui Le Cuong, Nguyen Van Quang
pmc-12554055.description: Introduction and importanceAcquired Hemophilia A (AHA) is a rare autoimmune bleeding disorder caused by autoantibodies against factor VIII. Diagnosis is often delayed when confounding factors coexist.Presentation of caseWe report a 70-year-old male with peripheral arterial disease presenting with critical limb ischemia, severe anemia, and prolonged APTT. Investigations revealed factor VIII inhibitor, concomitant factor XII deficiency, and lupus anticoagulant positivity.

pmc-13030792.creator: Xia Jing, Arild Faxvaag, Christian G. Nøhr, David Robinson, Paul G. Biondich, Timothy D. Law, Hua Min, Adam Wright, Yang Gong, Dean F. Sittig
pmc-13030792.description: Objectives: The objectives of this study were to educate the healthcare professional and the general public about interoperable vaccine records by elaborating on its definition, why we need one, what the challenges are, and what progress has been made in this direction.

pmc-13037106.title: f-SPION-mediated magnetic stimulation induces reparative Schwann cell reprogramming via cytoskeletal dynamics - gated activation of Piezo1
pmc-13037106.creator: Ting Liu, Mingxi Yang, Wantao Tian, Jingyan Ren, Laijin Lu, Yang Wang
pmc-13037106.description: BackgroundThe remarkable intrinsic regenerative capacity of peripheral nerves following injury is largely attributed to the phenotypic plasticity of Schwann cells (SCs) and their ability to transition into a repair-supportive state (rSCs). Transcriptional reprogramming of SCs into this reparative phenotype is pivotal for facilitating successful nerve regeneration.

pmc-13195880.title: Efficacy of PD-1 inhibitor plus induction chemotherapy for nasopharyngeal carcinoma with high-grade extranodal extension: a multicenter retrospective analysis
pmc-13195880.creator: Pingting Zhou, Xunmei Liu, Shuang Huang, Yunxiu Luo, Yuefeng Hu, Fapeng Wang, Rensheng Wang, Tingting Zhang
pmc-13195880.description: BackgroundsHigh-grade radiologic extranodal extension (G2/3-rENE) is a well-established adverse prognostic factor in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), as demonstrated in our previous research. This study aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of combining a PD-1 inhibitor with induction chemotherapy (IC) in this high-risk patient population.MethodsWe retrospectively analyzed 217 histologically confirmed non-metastatic NPC patients from three centers.

pmc-13317365.title: Natural diversity-guided catalytic-core chimerism engineers a rapid and inhibitor-tolerant reverse transcriptase
pmc-13317365.creator: Inês Fonseca Costa, Vânia Ondina Fernandes, Rita Silva Simões, Hélvio Simões, Virgínia Maria Rico Pires, Victor Diogo Alves, João Soeiro Teodoro, Pedro Bule, Carlos Mendes Godinho de Andrade Fontes
pmc-13317365.description: BackgroundReverse transcriptases (RTs) are essential components of RNA-based molecular technologies, yet their practical performance is often constrained by trade-offs between catalytic speed, thermal stability, and tolerance to inhibitory substances. Conventional optimization via mutagenesis or directed evolution often improves individual traits but struggles to integrate multiple traits within a single enzyme.
